why: I went through each verifier PASS/FAIL condition looking for anything stricter than its expect line and for checks that only read the diff. Check 1 runs the CLI on clean, bad-middle, mixed blank/torn and blank-only files and checks exit codes, line numbers and the `<file>:<line>: <error>` shape. It doesn't require any exact message text, only "a non-empty message". Check 2 only needs exit 2 and non-empty stderr. Check 3 imports and calls `lint`. Check 4 reads the package.json fields, runs `npm test` and reads the test files for coverage, and it allows extra args on the `node --test` script. Check 5 only needs to read files, and the line asks for nothing more. Check 6 asks for exactly one PR, the Closes line, a green workflow and a passing local `npm test`, all taken from the line. The mutation check is marked advisory, "not a pass/fail condition". There is no branch-name rule and no limit on which files the PR touches. The builder brief's extras (shebang, engines) are build steps, not pass/fail conditions.
